title: observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns + KV cache logging + dashboard/alert enhancements
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Added token-level cost & latency breakdown dashboards; KV cache hit/miss logging; tuned SLO alerts to reduce noise. No breaking API changes.
description:
Background: Production teams have asked for finer-grained observability to diagnose cost/latency regressions that only become visible at token granularity, and for better KV cache visibility to correlate cache behavior with token costs. This PR introduces token-level cost/latency metrics, additional KV cache logging, Grafana dashboards focused on per-route and per-model token economics, and alert tuning to reduce false positives.

What this change does: 
- Exposes token-level metrics: redwood.request.tokens.generated, redwood.request.tokens.prompt, redwood.request.token_latency.p50/p95/p99 (labels: model, route, customer_tier, quantization_profile). Metrics are emitted from the runtime's metrics bridge with cardinality controls.
- Adds KV cache metrics: redwood.kv_cache.hits, redwood.kv_cache.misses, redwood.kv_cache.ejection_count and a lightweight per-request KV probe log that can be enabled per-customer for debugging.
- Dashboard: New Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/token_cost_latency_dashboard.json) with panels for token cost breakdown, per-model latency percentiles, KV hit-rate heatmaps, and anomaly overlays.
- Alerts: Tuned alert rules to use aggregated error-budget windows and dynamic thresholds to reduce noise (rules/alerts/token_cost_alerts.yaml). Added alert annotations linking to runbooks.
- Logging: Introduced structured KV probe logs (when enabled) with sampling rate configuration to avoid high-cardinality logs.
- Tests: Unit tests for metric tagging, a small integration test that verifies KV metrics increment on a simulated cached request.

Motivation: Debugging high token-cost incidents often required expensive ad-hoc tracing or customer repros. Token-level telemetry plus KV visibility lets SREs and platform engineers attribute cost to model behavior (generation length, truncation, repeats) and to cache effectiveness.

Risk & mitigation: Higher metric cardinality and logging risk. Mitigations included: label whitelisting, sampling for probe logs, rate-limited metric emitters, and a feature flag to enable the richer logs per-tenant. Changes default to off for high-cardinality features.

Notes for reviewers: 
- Check the label whitelist in metrics/label_whitelist.go (we intentionally avoid user-provided freeform tags).
- Verify the alert tuning thresholds - they were derived from 90 days of histogram baselines; see ENG-1987 for analysis links.
- KV probe logging is gated behind config: observability.kv_probe.enabled. The default sample rate is 0.01 (1%) to limit cost.

Checklist: 
- [x] Metrics instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [x] Dashboards exported and reviewed with monitoring team
- [x] Alerts tuned and runbook links added
- [x] KV logging gated and sampled
- [x] Backwards-compatible and feature-flagged

Related: ENG-1987, ENG-2034, SUP-412

changelog_entry: Observability: Add token-level cost/latency metrics, KV cache metrics and sampled probe logs; new dashboards and tuned alerts (no breaking changes).
safety_and_mitigation: Metrics cardinality guarded via label whitelist; KV probe logging sampled by default; heavy features disabled by default and require config opt-in.
